summary.intent: Open and land the leftover-fixes PR (#240) for the Callisto release manager, then resolve the open question about nested Cargo workspaces (a Cargo workspace rooted below the repo root) and implement support for it.
summary.outcome: PR #240 was opened with CI green. After the user agreed to first-party Cargo workspace-root discovery, the assistant implemented per-root reads, writes, lockfile refresh/staging and nested membership in a new worktree (cargo-roots). It passed local `just ci` (92.66%) and was committed, but not yet pushed or opened as a PR.

repo: Callisto assumed every ecosystem's workspace root is the Callisto root. The assumption appeared in OpenContext, membership, inherited-dependency writes, lockfile refresh and historical reads. Nested Cargo workspaces with `version.workspace = true` therefore failed with E313.
Only Cargo resolves package fields from a parent manifest (`.workspace = true`). npm, pnpm and uv have only lockfile and membership nesting concerns.

Historical reads cannot use `cargo metadata` because past commits aren't checked out. Callisto must discover the enclosing root from Git objects, so discovery stays first-party and is bounded by the Callisto root.
Callisto already depends on the cargo binary for publishing (`registry_argv.rs`, ADR 0010), but TOML editing stays first-party because Cargo offers no format-preserving writes (ADR 0008).
Cargo discovery rules were verified against real Cargo: honor `package.workspace = "path"`, otherwise walk up to the nearest `[workspace]`. A real-Cargo oracle test was added.
Git exit codes (verified against real git): `rev-parse --verify --quiet` 1 means absent and 128 means failure. `git grep -l` 1 means no match. `git show rev:path` missing gives 128.
Workspace root detection requires a Git repository (E191), so the old `list_tags` 'not a git repository' tolerance was dead code.
A new test hit E101 SharedDefaultTagTemplate until the packages were given an explicit shared tag_template.

code.finding: Inherited-dependency writes load `workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml")`, a single-root assumption that blocked nested Cargo workspaces.
`OpenContext` held a single `cargo_workspace` loaded from `<root>/Cargo.toml`. This was the core single-root assumption, later replaced by per-root discovery.
`refresh_lockfiles` runs `cargo update --workspace` and checks for `Cargo.lock` at the repo root. It was made per Cargo workspace root.
Registry argv construction assumed the root Cargo workspace and was migrated to `load_at`.
`normalize_pattern` makes `./packages/*` and `packages/*/` match the same directories as `packages/*`. Nested-workspace membership was also added here.

workflow: The sandbox refuses heredocs and compound commands, so the working pattern is to write scripts with the Write tool and run them as files.
Piping `just ci` through `| tail` hid a failing exit code. Check the real exit status instead.
A `gh pr create` with a long, colon-containing title was refused by the guard, so a plain title was used.
Reproducing a reported concern with the real binary (and real cargo/git) before deciding clarified the problem and changed the recommendation twice.
Running `just ci` in the background while re-reading the diff avoids builds colliding with CI.

friction: Finding the earlier nested-workspace note took many transcript searches before it turned up as E313.
The first `just ci` failed on rustfmt, and the `| tail` pipe masked the failure.
Tool guards blocked a long PR title and compound shell commands, forcing workarounds.
Several old tests encoded the former tolerant behavior (list_tags without a repo, `commits_since` with a 128 fake) and had to be flipped.
The assistant's first recommendation (`cargo_metadata`) was reversed after reading the architecture, because historical reads can't use it.
open_items: Open and push the cargo-roots PR (committed locally, PR body drafted in scratchpad), and watch its CI.

Remaining Cargo-roots staging: per-root writes, per-root lockfile staging and historical reads were folded into this PR. Nested npm and uv roots get membership support only; their lockfile refresh is still root-bound.

Leftovers not yet done: shallow-clone guard, release-notes fallback, GitHub release body defaults, `has_explicit_table` ignoring inline/dotted `[workspace]` tables, pnpm detection mismatch, NAPI drift path guess, `cargo.rs` `bin_names`, and `relative_workspace_target` canonicalize `.ok()?`.

Deferred low findings recorded in PR #240: concurrent `add` race on name, one orphan non-commit tag stopping the whole workspace, `CliCommandRunner::run`/`run_with_stdin` blocking on pipe-holding descendants, persist replacing symlinks, `HEAD@{5}`-style since_ref giving a generic Git error, and `path_exists_at` erroring on `rev:./../x`.

Unresolved owner decisions: PyPI index serving no sha256, Python-only workspaces moving to the sealed CI route, worktree and branch cleanup, D01 ownership, trusted publishing (OIDC), and hosted verification (W11) of the generated build matrix.
Unverified assumption: whether the `cargo` binary is always present wherever load commands run. This matters less now that discovery stays first-party.
